subject: Re: Order Form — Annual Volume Discount & Minimum Commitment Safeguards
messages:
From: Anna Livingston <anna.livingston@acmehealth.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: TJ Brooks <tj.brooks@acmehealth.com>, legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form + pricing exhibit (redlines)

Hannah —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached are our procurement redlines to the Order Form and the Pricing Exhibit. A few items that are important for us to resolve before we route to finance/legal:

- Minimum annual commitment: we need a firm floor for year 1 (we propose $120k) tied to a stated consumption measurement.
- Volume discount triggers: we redlined tiers to ensure higher discounts kick in at 1M tokens and 5M tokens.
- Price protection / cap: procurement wants a 12-month price protection clause for any per-token increases.
- True-up mechanics: we proposed quarterly true-ups with a 30-day invoice window.

We attached a PDF with inline comments. Can you confirm which of these items you can accept versus items that require internal approvals?

We'd like to keep momentum — finance is aiming to finalize by 11/05.

Thanks,
Anna Livingston
Head of Procurement, Acme Health
anna.livingston@acmehealth.com
attachments: redlines_annotated.pdf, Pricing_Exhibit_Annex.pdf

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Livingston <anna.livingston@acmehealth.com>
Cc: TJ Brooks <tj.brooks@acmehealth.com>, markus_klein@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form + pricing exhibit (redlines)

Anna —

Appreciate the clear redlines and the timelines. Quick note on process: a few of these items (minimum commitment floors and price-protection language) are policy-level and I'll need sign-off from billing and legal. That said, we can move on the following immediately:

- Quarterly true-up with a 30-day invoice window — acceptable. I'll reflect that in the next iteration.
- Volume tiers — we can map the tiers you proposed to our tiering engine, but we need to confirm exact token definitions (prompt vs. completion).

Internal ask: Markus, Neha, Rishi — can you weigh in on the minimum-commitment floor and the 12-month price protection? Specifically: is a firm $120k first-year floor feasible and what guardrail language do we require for a price-protection cap?

Anna — I can prepare a clean Order Form with tracked changes and a short memo on the items that require escalation by tomorrow EOD. Does that work for your team?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(h) 415-555-0192
attachments: Acme_OrderForm_v2.docx (will update after internal review)

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form + pricing exhibit (redlines)

Hannah — quick internal on the three escalations Anna flagged:

1) Minimum annual commitment (floor):
- We can accept a firm Year 1 floor at $120k if the customer agrees to a quarterly true-up and a rolling 12-month lookback for consumption adjustments. Need this documented as: "Customer commits to a minimum annual spend of $120,000 for Term Year 1; usage overage will be invoiced per the Pricing Exhibit and true-ups applied quarterly."

2) Volume discount triggers:
- Tier thresholds are OK, but we need an explicit definition: "Tokens" defined as "input + output tokens measured by Redwood's tokenization engine as of the Effective Date." Avoid ambiguous language that shifts measurement.

3) 12-month price protection / cap:
- We can't provide an absolute ceiling on Redwood's published list prices indefinitely. We can offer a 12-month 'price protection' for the per-token rate that applies only to the pricing exhibited in the Order Form and subject to a force-majeure/right-to-pass-through clause for third-party cost changes (e.g., cloud provider price hikes). Proposed language snippet: "Redwood will not increase the per-token rates set forth in the Pricing Exhibit for a period of 12 months from the Effective Date, except to the extent directly caused by third-party provider cost increases, or changes required by applicable law."

If Anna needs tighter language (e.g., absolute cap without carveouts), this will require RevOps + Legal sign-off and likely a concession elsewhere (longer minimum commitment or higher upfront payment).

Neha, Rishi — please confirm if we want to attach an upsell credit for a 24-month ramp if customer opts into a 24-month committed term.

Markus
VP, North America Sales (internal)

From: TJ Brooks <tj.brooks@acmehealth.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Anna Livingston <anna.livingston@acmehealth.com>, legal@acmehealth.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form + pricing exhibit (redlines)

Hannah / Markus —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the proposed language. A couple of quick points from Acme Legal that will help us close:

- The 12-month protection with the third-party carve is acceptable if the wording is narrow — we will accept a carve for "statutorily mandated tax or fee increases" but not for broad "cloud provider" cost changes unless substantiated by invoice evidence.
- For the minimum commitment floor, Acme can accept $120k for Year 1 but asks that any unused portion be eligible for a one-time credit to Year 2 if we increase committed capacity to a 24-month term.

If you can send a final clean Order Form and a DocuSign envelope with the revised Pricing Exhibit and the short concession language, procurement will push to sign this week.

DocuSign routing requested: anna.livingston@acmehealth.com -> tj.brooks@acmehealth.com -> legal@acmehealth.com

Thanks,
TJ Brooks
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Health
attachments: none
